transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because… it’s been going on for months, and I feel like nobody is really hearing me. My husband’s family has been quietly messing with things—our money, our reputation, just little things that add up. Like at work, I’m a billing clerk, so I notice when numbers don’t look right, and then people act like it’s just some harmless error. But it’s not random.

And then at church, someone will suddenly be cold to me, or look at me funny, and I know something’s been said. It all ties back to them somehow. Even when people pull up records and say, “See, everything looks normal,” I know what I’m seeing. It’s too many little things to be a coincidence.
Have you had a period when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

Unusually energetic? I don’t know… I mean, I get tired like anyone else. Sometimes I stay up thinking about things, but that’s not like I’m full of energy, it’s more just… my mind won’t settle. And sleep is hard to judge because if something’s going on around you, of course you’re not going to sleep perfectly. But no, I don’t think I’ve had some big stretch where I didn’t need sleep or anything like that.
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?

Voices? I mean… not like someone standing in the room talking to me, if that’s what you mean. Sometimes I’ll hear people talking low, like in another room or outside, and I’ll try to catch what they’re saying, but that’s just… you know, when you live in a neighborhood and people don’t always mind their business. 

But no, I don’t think I’ve heard a voice when nobody was there.
When people show you proof that your husband’s family is not interfering, are you able to consider that you might be mistaken?

I mean, I listen to what they’re saying, but records don’t show everything. People act like if a paper says it’s fine, then that proves nothing is happening, but I work with billing, I know how little things can be made to look normal. And it’s not just one thing—it’s the money stuff, then someone at church suddenly treats me different, and you can feel when your name’s been dragged around.

So… no, I don’t really think I’m mistaken. I think people just don’t want to see how it all connects back to his family.
Have you ever felt that other people could put thoughts into your mind?

Put thoughts into my mind? No, I don’t mean it like that. It’s not like somebody is placing words in my head.

What I’m saying is, for months I’ve been trying to get people to see that my husband’s family is interfering in ways that look small if you take them one at a time. Like a little billing error at work, or someone at church suddenly acting strange toward me, and everybody says, “Oh, that’s just a mistake,” but it’s not just one thing. It keeps happening, and it all points back to them messing with our money and our good name.

So no, not thoughts in my mind. More like they’re working around me, quietly.
Have you noticed that your emotions feel flatter than they used to?

Flatter? I don’t know… I mean, I get tired, sure. Anybody would, with work and then coming home and trying to keep everything straight. Some days I probably don’t react the way people expect me to, but that doesn’t mean I don’t feel things.

Like at work, if someone makes a joke, maybe I don’t laugh as much because I’m thinking about the posting reports or what still has to be fixed before the end of the day. People take that the wrong way sometimes. So… I haven’t really noticed my emotions being flat, no. I’m just worn out sometimes.
Have these concerns caused you to do worse at work or in taking care of things at home?

I mean, not really in the way people make it sound. I still get up and go to work, I do my billing and posting like I’m supposed to. I’m not just sitting around letting everything fall apart. At home I keep things going too—laundry, meals, the usual things. I still get out in the garden when I can, and sometimes I paint, though I’ll admit my mind wanders.

The trouble is more when I try to tell people what’s going on with my in-laws. That’s when things get tense, because people act like I’m causing a problem just by warning them. But my actual work and the house? I’m handling them.
Have you tended to distrust people and suspect they have harmful intentions toward you for most of your adult life?

Most of my adult life? I don’t know if I’d put it that way. I mean, I’ve always tried to be careful with people, but doesn’t everybody? You learn, especially at work, that if a number is off by even a little bit, it can turn into a whole mess, and then people start asking who touched what file.

But harmful intentions… I’m not sure. Some people are just careless, or they gossip, and that can do plenty of damage without them planning it. I wouldn’t say I’ve gone around my whole life thinking everyone was out to hurt me. That sounds stronger than what I mean.
Have you ever felt that someone was controlling your actions?

Controlling my actions… no, not like making my arms move or anything like that. I’m still the one doing what I do.

But it feels like they’re controlling what happens around me, if that makes sense. My husband’s family has been quietly messing with our money and our good name for months now. Like, a little billing error shows up at work and suddenly I’m the one feeling watched, or someone at church acts strange toward me out of nowhere. And then people say, “Well, the records don’t show that,” but records don’t show everything. I know it ties back to them somehow.
Besides your husband’s family, have you had the feeling that ordinary events around you carry a special message meant specifically for you?

I don’t know about “special messages” exactly. It’s more that things happen and people act like they’re separate, but they’re not. Like I’ve been trying for months to get people to see that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name.

A little billing error shows up at work, or someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me, and everybody wants to say, “Oh, that’s just a mistake,” or “maybe they were having a bad day.” But then records get pulled and they say there’s no proof, like paperwork tells the whole story. It doesn’t. I know it ties back to them somehow.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?

Not really… I mean, sometimes people tell me I give too much background before I get to the point. My supervisor used to say, “Just tell me the invoice number,” but you can’t always understand the invoice number without knowing who entered it first and whether the account had an adjustment before that.

But hard to follow? I don’t know. Maybe when I’m upset I explain things in a roundabout way. I try to be clear.
Have you ever felt that an outside force was controlling your thoughts?

An outside force controlling my thoughts? No… I don’t think so. My thoughts are mine. I mean, I can get stuck thinking about things, especially when something doesn’t add up, but that’s just me trying to sort it out.

Like when people say, “Don’t worry about it,” I can’t just stop, because if an account is off by even a small amount, you have to trace where it started. That’s how I was trained. But nobody is putting thoughts in my head or steering them, if that’s what you mean.
Have you seen things that other people could not see?

Seen things? Like… things that weren’t there? I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve noticed things other people miss, but that’s different.

Like at work, if a number is off or someone changed something in the system, other people will walk right past it because they’re in a hurry or they don’t want to get involved. But that’s not me seeing something nobody else could see, it’s just… paying attention. So no, not in that way.
Do you ever feel that your thoughts are being broadcast so that other people can know what you are thinking?

No, I don’t think people can hear my thoughts or anything like that. I mean, sometimes it feels like people guess what I’m thinking, especially if they’ve worked with you long enough — like at my old job, people knew I was going to bring up a billing issue before I even said it, because I always noticed those things.

But that’s not the same as my thoughts being… broadcast. I don’t think that happens.
Do you believe your husband’s family has any impossible or supernatural way of influencing events around you?

Impossible or supernatural? No, I wouldn’t say it like that. They’re not casting spells or anything. It’s more… people know people, and things get said, and then suddenly our money is off or my name gets dragged through something.

I’ve been trying for months to get people to understand that his family is quietly behind it. Like a little billing error shows up at work, and everybody acts like it’s just a mistake, but I know how those things happen. Or someone at church gets funny with me all at once, like they’ve heard something. And then people pull records and say, “See, there’s nothing there,” but records don’t show everything. They don’t show who started it. So no, not supernatural, but they have ways of influencing things.
Have you found yourself talking much less than you used to?

I don’t think so… I mean, I’ve always talked when I have something to say. Some people think I talk too much if I’m trying to explain something properly, especially if they don’t want to hear the details.

At work, for example, if there was an issue with a payment posting, you can’t just say one sentence and expect people to understand it. You have to explain where the number came from, who touched it, what got changed. So I don’t know if I’m talking less. Maybe around certain people I don’t bother as much, because they’ve already made up their mind. But I haven’t noticed myself going quiet in general.
Have you been completely convinced that your husband’s family is deliberately trying to harm your money or reputation?

Yes. I mean, I’m not saying they stand there and announce it, but I’m convinced they’re behind it. That’s why I’m here, honestly, because for months I’ve been trying to get people to see it.

Little things happen — like billing errors showing up at work, or somebody at church suddenly treating me strange — and everyone says, “Oh, that’s just a mistake,” or “Maybe you’re reading into it.” But when it keeps happening, and it’s always around our money or our good name, you start to know where it’s coming from.

And people can pull records all day long, but records don’t show who whispered what or who started it. They don’t show that part. So yes, I do believe his family is deliberately doing it, quietly.
For how long have you been convinced that your husband’s family is deliberately trying to harm your money or reputation?

About nine months, I’d say. It really started after that trouble with my husband’s family over money and what everyone expected around the holidays.

And holidays are always when people show who they are, you know? They act like it’s about dinner or gifts or whose house you go to, but then somehow it turns into who paid for what and who owes who. After that, things just kept happening, and I couldn’t ignore the pattern anymore. So… yes, about nine months.

I don’t think so… I mean, I’ve always talked when I have something to say. Some people think I talk too much if I’m trying to explain something properly, especially if they don’t want to hear the details.

At work, for example, if there was an issue with a payment posting, you can’t just say one sentence and expect people to understand it. You have to explain where the number came from, who touched it, what got changed. So I don’t know if I’m talking less. Maybe around certain people I don’t bother as much, because they’ve already made up their mind. But I haven’t noticed myself going quiet in general.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been sustained non-bizarre persecutory delusion without other core schizophrenic symptoms, which would favor delusional disorder over schizophrenia-spectrum alternatives.
doctor.question: Have you been completely convinced that your husband’s family is deliberately trying to harm your money or reputation?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name, like when little billing errors show up at work or someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me, and no matter what records anyone pulls up I know it ties back to them.
target_item.reason: The question directly asks about being completely convinced of a fixed belief that the husband’s family is deliberately harming her money or reputation, which matches the delusions profile.

patient.answer:
Yes. I mean, I’m not saying they stand there and announce it, but I’m convinced they’re behind it. That’s why I’m here, honestly, because for months I’ve been trying to get people to see it.

Little things happen — like billing errors showing up at work, or somebody at church suddenly treating me strange — and everyone says, “Oh, that’s just a mistake,” or “Maybe you’re reading into it.” But when it keeps happening, and it’s always around our money or our good name, you start to know where it’s coming from.

And people can pull records all day long, but records don’t show who whispered what or who started it. They don’t show that part. So yes, I do believe his family is deliberately doing it, quietly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief has lasted at least 3 months, which best distinguishes persistent delusional disorder from acute/transient psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: For how long have you been convinced that your husband’s family is deliberately trying to harm your money or reputation?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about nine months, ever since the trouble with my husband’s family over money and holiday expectations.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the belief has been present, which directly matches the duration item.

patient.answer:
About nine months, I’d say. It really started after that trouble with my husband’s family over money and what everyone expected around the holidays.

And holidays are always when people show who they are, you know? They act like it’s about dinner or gifts or whose house you go to, but then somehow it turns into who paid for what and who owes who. After that, things just kept happening, and I couldn’t ignore the pattern anymore. So… yes, about nine months.

inference.note: Fixed persecutory delusion present for about 9 months with preserved functioning and no evidence of hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal/broadcasting, passivity phenomena, disorganization, negative symptoms, mania, or lifelong pervasive suspiciousness. This rules against F23.3, F20.0, and F60.0.
